title: The One With The Sharks

jokes.text: Phoebe walks into Central Perk with her dress unzipped, complaining no one offered to zip her up between apartments
jokes.setup: Phoebe asks Ross to zip up her dress and thanks him
jokes.punchline: She laments that nobody between her apartment and here offered to do it — implying she walked through New York with her dress unzipped expecting strangers to zip her up
jokes.explanation: Classic Phoebe — the joke works because it reveals her worldview: she genuinely expected strangers to zip her up. The 'People.' dismissal from Ross adds a dry topper. Strong character integration.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Could you zip me up?

dialogue.speaker: Other Character
dialogue.line: Of course.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: You know, it's so sad. You go out on the street, and nobody just zips up your dress for you anymore. What happened to society?

jokes.text: "Am I ready to take my Grade A loins off the meat market?"
jokes.setup: Ross asks if Phoebe's relationship with Mike is getting serious
jokes.punchline: Phoebe refers to herself as 'Grade A loins' on a 'meat market' — an absurdly carnivorous metaphor delivered with total sincerity
jokes.explanation: The joke lands on the specific word 'loins' — a deliberately unusual word that makes the dating-market metaphor both funnier and very Phoebe. High character integration; she would use this exact phrasing.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: I mean, my body's like a meat market. Guys come in, they look around, they poke the ribs, they move on to the next thing.

jokes.text: "You are a bit of a drama queen."
jokes.setup: Ross explains his anxious approach to relationships — 'Is this moving too fast? Too slow? Where is this going?'
jokes.punchline: Phoebe calls him a drama queen mid-complaint, with zero self-awareness given her own dramatic tendencies
jokes.explanation: Functional joke that works as a quick character beat. Phoebe calling anyone a drama queen is mildly ironic, but the joke is a bit easy and doesn't fully commit to the irony.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Yeah, you do.

jokes.text: Ross gradually realizes Phoebe has never been in a long-term relationship — the dawning horror on his face as he encourages her
jokes.setup: Ross is praising Phoebe for casually dating without worrying about things getting serious
jokes.punchline: He realizes mid-compliment that she actually CAN'T get into a serious relationship — his praise is accidentally devastating
jokes.explanation: The comedy is in the structure: Ross's compliment slowly inverts into an accidental insult as both characters realize the truth. Well-constructed beat for a sitcom cold open.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Okay, so you're saying you've never been in a serious relationship?

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: That's right.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: What about... what about that guy, um, the one with the—

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Nope.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Okay, but surely there was... I mean, what about—

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Nope.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Oh my God. You're actually right. You've never had a serious relationship.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: I know.

jokes.text: "At least you've been married. Oh, my God! I want to trade lives with Ross?!"
jokes.setup: Ross says Phoebe doesn't strike him as someone who wants to get married; she insists she does, and he apologizes by noting he's been divorced three times
jokes.punchline: Phoebe envies his divorces, then immediately horrifies herself by realizing she wants to trade lives with Ross — the least enviable Friend
jokes.explanation: One of the episode's best jokes. The two-step structure is excellent: (1) Phoebe envies the divorces, which is funny on its own; (2) she immediately clocks how pathetic that desire is. The self-awareness in real time — 'I want to trade lives with Ross?!' — is both very Phoebe and a great joke about Ross's status among the group. High quotability, well-earned.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: You've been married three times?!

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: And I'm the one who wants to trade lives with you?!

jokes.text: Phoebe asks 'How do I look?' while visibly crying, then asks for a compact
jokes.setup: Mike arrives to pick Phoebe up for a date; she's been crying
jokes.punchline: She asks 'How do I look?' presumably while tear-streaked, then needs a compact — the physical reality undercuts her attempt to seem fine
jokes.explanation: Functional visual gag dependent on the performance. Works as a topper to the cold open's emotional beats, but the joke itself is fairly basic.

dialogue.speaker: Mike
dialogue.line: Do you have a compact? I want to check how I look.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: No, I don't.

dialogue.speaker: Mike
dialogue.line: Oh, well... you look great.

jokes.text: "But if her face is as nice as her ass... Mama!"
jokes.setup: Rachel has just agreed to evaluate the woman
jokes.punchline: She sees the woman's face, says 'Mama!' — a Joey-style exclamation coming from the usually more refined Rachel
jokes.explanation: The 'Mama!' reaction works because it's Joey's vocabulary coming out of Rachel's mouth, suggesting the woman corrupted even Rachel's standards. Mild laugh, nothing exceptional.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: I'm not going to sit here and objectify women with you, Joey.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Come on, Mon, it's harmless.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: No. I have principles.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Look at her! Look at her!

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: I'm not— Okay, fine, where? Oh my God, did you see the way she walked by?

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: I know!

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: That was incredible! And those shoes? Those shoes were amazing!

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Hey, guys.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Nothing! We weren't doing anything!

jokes.text: "Damn it. I'm gonna have to start listening when he talks about his job."
jokes.setup: Monica explains that Chandler has to stay in Tulsa for work but she doesn't know why
jokes.punchline: She admits she's never actually listened to Chandler talk about his job — delivered as a resigned epiphany
jokes.explanation: Economical and sharp. The joke lands on the casual self-awareness — Monica isn't embarrassed, just mildly inconvenienced by this realization. Plays on the running gag that nobody knows what Chandler does for a living, including his wife.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: I don't know what Chandler does.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: What do you mean you don't know what he does?

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: I don't know! He has a job and he goes to an office, but I honestly have no idea what he does there.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Does he work with numbers?

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Maybe? I tune out whenever he starts talking about it.

jokes.text: "You should bring your black see-through teddy with the attached garters." "How do you know I have one of those?" "Didn't until just now."
jokes.setup: Joey suggests Monica wear something sexy for the Tulsa surprise visit
jokes.punchline: Monica asks how he knew about the specific lingerie; he reveals he was fishing — and she just confirmed it exists
jokes.explanation: Tight three-line structure with a clean misdirect. The joke turns on Monica walking into Joey's trap, which is very Joey — using apparent knowledge to fish for real information. Excellent economy (the punchline is five words), and the moment rewards attention. One of the stronger jokes in the episode.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: You should wear that black lace thing when Chandler comes over.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: How did you know about that?

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: I didn't. I was just fishing.

jokes.text: Joey blurts 'Hot!' at a woman, is confronted, and says he thought she heard 'hi'
jokes.setup: Joey evaluates an attractive woman's appearance out loud without meaning to
jokes.punchline: 'I said that I think you're hot. And... now I'm embarrassed. I thought you said hi.' — his attempt at recovery is to claim he heard a 'hi' that didn't exist
jokes.explanation: Joey's cringe-worthy bluntness followed by his half-assed cover story is very on-brand. The 'I'll try that — hi, I'm Joey' topper is a nice beat. Functional character comedy.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Oh wow, she's hot.

dialogue.speaker: Woman
dialogue.line: Excuse me?

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: I said... uh... you're... a lot? A lot of... fun?

jokes.text: Hayley pre-empts Joey's date invitation before he actually asks: "I would love to go out with you." "Really? Great. Did I — did I actually ask you?"
jokes.setup: Joey is building toward asking Hayley out but hasn't gotten there yet
jokes.punchline: She accepts before he asks; his genuine confusion about whether he actually asked is the punchline
jokes.explanation: Good reversal — the woman takes control of Joey's routine, which is unexpected. His confusion is genuine and the follow-up 'That's just where you were going. I figured I'd help you out' is a nice beat that makes her charming too.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: So, would you maybe want to grab coffee at one of those cool coffeehouses?

dialogue.speaker: Hayley
dialogue.line: Bless you.

jokes.text: "You should see someone about that cold. If it gets much worse, you could die."
jokes.setup: Hayley sneezes during conversation with Joey
jokes.punchline: Joey treats a mild sneeze as a potentially fatal symptom — with complete sincerity
jokes.explanation: Joey's oblivious hypochondria-by-proxy is funny. The deadpan delivery of a melodramatic medical warning for a sneeze is a good Joey beat. Slight but effective.

jokes.text: "Would you call this girl: 'Thanks for... a lovely... evening'?" — Ross miming a tearful phone call
jokes.setup: Phoebe says Mike hasn't called after their terrible date where she cried repeatedly
jokes.punchline: She demonstrates exactly what a call from her would have sounded like — a sobbing, halting 'Thanks for a lovely evening' — implying any sane person would run
jokes.explanation: Visual performance joke that works well — the specific cadence of the imagined call is funny, and the implied self-awareness (she's a disaster date) gives it dimension.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: I think I'm coming down with something. I've been sneezing all day.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: It's just a cold, man.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Just a cold? Chandler, I can feel it getting worse. My throat is closing up.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Have you tried some soup?

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Soup won't help me now. I can barely breathe. This is it. This is how it ends.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Oh my God, Joey, you're going to be fine.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: No, I'm not. I'm dying. I'm actually dying right now.

jokes.text: "You know how hard it is to meet a guy like that? We are a rare breed."
jokes.setup: Phoebe laments that Mike was sweet, smart, and funny — a rare find
jokes.punchline: Ross immediately inserts himself into the category of 'sweet, smart, and funny' men — implying he's also a rare catch, despite being famously unlucky in love
jokes.explanation: Modest self-congratulation from Ross is a reliable character note. Slight joke that gets a chuckle but isn't memorable.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: He's gonna call. He's definitely gonna call. He'll probably call tomorrow. Or the next day. Or... maybe not for like a week. But then he'll call. And he'll be like, 'Hey Phoebe, it's Mike.' And I'll be like, 'Oh, Mike! Hi!' And he'll be like, 'Yeah, so... how have you been?' And I'll be like, 'Good! I've been good.' And then there'll be this long silence. And he'll be like, 'So... do you wanna get coffee or something?' And I'll be like, 'Sure, that sounds nice.' And then we'll go get coffee. And it'll be nice. But also kind of awkward.

jokes.text: Joey's internal monologue narrating his date: "So this is going pretty good. Dinner was nice. We've got a lot in common. Victoria's Secret. We even like the same books."
jokes.setup: Joey is on a date and cataloguing what they have in common
jokes.punchline: 'Victoria's Secret' is listed flatly between normal shared interests — implying it's a magazine they both enjoy, or simply that he noticed her lingerie, with zero self-consciousness
jokes.explanation: The joke is in the flat listing — 'dinner was nice... Victoria's Secret... same books.' The non-sequitur dropped in without emphasis is a good piece of comedic economy. Very Joey: he sees nothing odd about cataloguing lingerie as a shared interest. Strong character integration.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Good guys are hard to find.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Ross, you've dated like half of New York.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Yeah, well, none of them worked out!

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Because you're not a good guy, Ross.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: What? I'm a great guy!

jokes.text: "There's a scary painting. Wait a minute. I think I've been scared by that painting before."
jokes.setup: Joey begins to notice his date's apartment looks familiar
jokes.punchline: His specific memory trigger is the painting — not her face, not the furniture, but the scary painting. This reveals both how superficial his memory is and how distinctive the painting must be.
jokes.explanation: Good joke structure: the painting as the memory trigger is both specific and revealing. Joey recognizes the apartment before he recognizes the person — a great character detail. The escalation over the next few lines makes this the start of an excellent extended beat.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Thank you so much for letting me have the last piece of cake.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: So, you got any more cake at your place?

jokes.text: "Oh, my God. I've gone out with this girl before. Yeah! We had sex on this couch! And then on that chair, and — No. No, we didn't do it here... which is weird, because it seems like a perfectly good place."
jokes.setup: Joey realizes he's been in this apartment and slept with this woman before
jokes.punchline: He mentally surveys each piece of furniture for prior sexual activity, then notes with genuine architectural puzzlement that one spot was overlooked — implying regret at the missed opportunity
jokes.explanation: One of the episode's best jokes. The escalation from 'I've been here before' to a mental furniture inventory of past sexual encounters is funny, and the topper — genuine confusion about the one spot they missed, delivered as an interior design observation — is inspired. Only Joey would react this way. High character integration, strong structure, well-earned laugh. Comparable to an 8-range joke.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Oh my God, this painting is creepy.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Wait a minute... I know this place. I've been here before!

jokes.text: "Unless... you're not gonna try and get me to join a cult, are you?"
jokes.setup: Ross shows up at Mike's door saying he 'really, really needs to talk to him about something'
jokes.punchline: Mike's first concern is that this is a cult recruitment visit
jokes.explanation: The absurd left-field guess subverts the expected response to an earnest stranger. Mild but effective.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: We did it on the couch, we did it in the kitchen, we did it in the bathroom...

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: But we never did it in the closet.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: [looks confused at the closet]

jokes.text: "You know, it's just, you have that look." "Damn Supercuts!"
jokes.setup: Mike wonders why Ross thought he looked like a cult recruiter
jokes.punchline: Ross says Mike has 'that look'; Mike immediately blames his budget haircut chain — confirming the unflattering assessment while also being self-deprecating
jokes.explanation: 'Damn Supercuts!' is two words and a curse that lands a full joke. The specificity of Supercuts (not just 'a cheap haircut') makes it sharper and funnier. Great economy, good as a one-liner. Very quotable.

dialogue.speaker: Mike
dialogue.line: Are you recruiting for a cult?

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: No, why would you say that?

dialogue.speaker: Mike
dialogue.line: You just have that cult-like appearance.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: It's just my cheap haircut.

jokes.text: "Well, then I didn't need to bother you. You or the four other Mike Hanigans I bothered."
jokes.setup: Ross learns Mike has already called Phoebe — his intervention was unnecessary
jokes.punchline: He casually reveals he tracked down five people named Mike Hanigan to deliver this message — an absurdly disproportionate response
jokes.explanation: The delivery of 'four other Mike Hanigans' as a throwaway afterthought is what makes this exceptional. The joke rewards the audience for imagining the four other confrontations. Very Ross — his obsessive thoroughness taken to an absurd extreme. Strong character integration and economy.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Wait, you're not the Mike Hanigan I was looking for.

dialogue.speaker: Mike
dialogue.line: There's more than one?

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Yeah, I talked to like five of you guys before I found the right one.

jokes.text: Ross admits he visited five different Mike Hanigans before finding the right one
jokes.setup: Ross is wrapping up his mission accomplished visit to Mike.
jokes.punchline: 'You or the four other Mike Hanigans I bothered.' — Ross's obsessive interference required hunting down five people named Mike Hanigan.
jokes.explanation: The reveal that Ross bothered four other innocent men named Mike Hanigan is a great escalation of his oblivious meddling. The specificity ('four other Mike Hanigans') is the key — it implies a whole absurd subplot of apologetic visits. Well-economized.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: I was just... I was just trying to say that um, that Rachel is a very... uh... a very well-thought-out young woman. And that, uh, her eyes are like two shimmering pools of... of gorgeous blue-green... ness.

jokes.text: Ross's rambling attempt to un-tell Mike about Phoebe's relationship history: "I will also say... what I'm about to say... vis-à-vis... the following."
jokes.setup: Ross is trying to cover his tracks and invent a fake relationship for Phoebe
jokes.punchline: His stalling — drowning in throat-clearing filler phrases — is the joke; the audience sees him failing to think on his feet in real time
jokes.explanation: Physical/verbal comedy dependent on performance. The 'vis-à-vis... the following' is a great pompous stall. Works as a character beat but the transcript alone undersells it — this is a performance joke.

dialogue.speaker: Mike
dialogue.line: Vikram? That's an unusual name.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Unusual? That's the unbelievable part? Not that I'm dating someone named Vikram, but that the name itself is unusual?

jokes.text: "Phoebe has never had a serious relationship since... her super-serious relationship... with... Vikram." "Vikram?" "What? That's a real name."
jokes.setup: Ross is making up a fake ex-boyfriend's name on the spot
jokes.punchline: He lands on 'Vikram' — clearly not his first choice — and defensively pre-empts skepticism by confirming it is a real name
jokes.explanation: 'That's a real name' is the punchline doing all the work — it's Ross defending his made-up choice preemptively, which reveals he knows exactly how suspicious it sounds. The specificity of 'Vikram' as his desperate improvisation is funnier than any generic name would be. Well-constructed, very quotable.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: I could go to the gym, or I could stay in and watch something educational...

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Nah, porn it is.

jokes.text: Ross's invented boyfriend's name: 'Vikram.' Mike: 'Vikram?' Ross: 'What? That's a real name.'
jokes.setup: Ross invents a fake serious boyfriend for Phoebe, needing a name on the spot.
jokes.punchline: 'Vikram.' — the name lands as so random that Mike questions it, and Ross defensively confirms it's real.
jokes.explanation: Perfect economy. The name 'Vikram' lands as both random and oddly specific — Ross's brain lands on an unusual but defensible name, and his subsequent 'What? That's a real name' is the ideal defensive punchline. The exchange is tight, specific, and very quotable. The name 'Vikram' recurs throughout the episode and pays off beautifully.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Chandler! What are you doing?

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: What? I'm just watching TV. Regular TV. Very normal, regular television programming.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Uh-huh.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: It's a documentary. Very educational. About... sports.

jokes.text: Chandler alone in his Tulsa hotel room: "Stop it! Why couldn't they have sent me to Texas? Seven o'clock. Maybe I'll hit the gym."
jokes.setup: Chandler is alone and bored in a Tulsa hotel room on a Friday night
jokes.punchline: He talks himself out of his loneliness, briefly considers the gym (a comically optimistic notion), and immediately abandons it
jokes.explanation: Setup for the pay-per-view punchline. Works as a Chandler beat — the gym suggestion is immediately recognizable as a lie he's telling himself.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: You won't believe what I just walked in on. Chandler was in the living room with a shark documentary, and he was... he was really into it.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: What do you mean 'really into it'?

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: I mean he had candles lit, rose petals on the floor, and he kept saying 'Oh baby, show me those teeth.'

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: No! Chandler has a shark fetish?

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Apparently!

jokes.text: "Who am I kidding? Pay-per-view porn."
jokes.setup: Chandler considers going to the gym to fill his lonely hotel night
jokes.punchline: He immediately drops the pretense — the real plan was always pay-per-view porn
jokes.explanation: Economical and funny. 'Who am I kidding? Pay-per-view porn.' is four words of punchline after one word of self-awareness. Sets up the entire shark subplot efficiently. The directness is disarming and funny.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Monica, do you remember your marriage vows?

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Of course I do.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Well, you promised to love, honor, and cherish Chandler. That means some things are acceptable in a marriage and some things aren't.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: What are you saying?

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: I'm saying there's a hierarchy. Like, him forgetting your birthday? Unacceptable. Him leaving the toilet seat up? Unacceptable. But him spending all your money on a stupid boat? Actually, that's still unacceptable.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: He didn't buy a boat!

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: I know, I'm just saying if he did, you'd have bigger problems than the toilet seat.

jokes.text: Monica bursts in with "Surprise!" as Chandler dives for the remote
jokes.setup: Chandler is watching pay-per-view porn in his hotel room; Monica surprise-visits
jokes.punchline: His frantic channel-switching and 'Do not disturb!' just before she opens the door — the audience knows exactly what he's doing
jokes.explanation: Classic sitcom situation — perfectly timed interruption. The comedy is fully in the performance and the audience's shared knowledge. Functional but not exceptional writing.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: So this guy, he has like the weirdest fantasies. I mean, he wants to do it on a dinosaur or something.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: A dinosaur? Rachel, that's... wait. What does he do for a living?

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: He's a paleontologist.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Oh my God. That's my brother!

jokes.text: "I was just... watching some regular television there. What a pleasant surprise."
jokes.setup: Monica has just walked in; Chandler has hastily changed the channel
jokes.punchline: His cover story — 'regular television' — and the forced 'What a pleasant surprise' are transparently guilty
jokes.explanation: 'Regular television' is a good guilty-euphemism. The joke depends on the transparent cover attempt, which is a Chandler specialty.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: I'm very memorable in bed. Women remember me.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Joey, how would you know that?

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Well, you'd have to sleep with me to find out.

jokes.text: "I just got to Chandler's room, and I caught him... molesting himself." "That couldn't have been pretty."
jokes.setup: Monica calls Rachel to report what she found in the hotel room
jokes.punchline: Rachel's matter-of-fact response — 'That couldn't have been pretty' — treats it as an unfortunate-but-unsurprising visual rather than a scandal
jokes.explanation: Rachel's callback is the best part — the casual, resigned 'That couldn't have been pretty' is a great deadpan response. The word 'molesting' is a bit broad but the exchange works.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Look, I may have some bloated nights, okay? But I'm still better than most people!

jokes.text: "The weird part is... he was getting off... to a shark-attack show!" "Chandler watches shark porn!"
jokes.setup: Monica has established Chandler was masturbating; now she reveals the channel he was watching
jokes.punchline: He was watching a shark documentary — Rachel immediately coins the term 'shark porn'
jokes.explanation: The pivot from 'caught him masturbating' (expected) to 'to a shark documentary' (completely unexpected) is a strong misdirect. 'Shark porn' as Rachel's instant coinage is a great comic invention. The absurdity of the scenario — and the entire episode's shark running gag — originates here. High impact in a room setting.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: No more beans for me.

jokes.text: Rachel's reaction to 'Chandler watches shark porn!': 'While watching sharks?'
jokes.setup: Monica announces that Chandler has a shark fetish.
jokes.punchline: Rachel's clarifying question — 'While watching sharks?' — treats this as a logistical query rather than an expression of shock. The deadpan of it, as if confirming a mundane detail, is the joke.
jokes.explanation: A good tag on the shark revelation. Rachel's flat, confirmatory question treats the absurdity as a procedural detail, which is funnier than a bigger reaction would be.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Do you think sharks are sexy?

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: What? No! Why would I think sharks are sexy?

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Well, you think Ariel is sexy.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Ariel's a mermaid, Monica. That's completely different.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: She's half fish, Joey.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Yeah, but the top half is all woman!

jokes.text: "You promised to love him no matter what." "'What' means, like, if he gets a disease or kills someone. Not if he gets his jollies to Jaws."
jokes.setup: Rachel counsels Monica to be accepting; Monica pushes back
jokes.punchline: Monica's legal parsing of wedding vows — 'what' has specific limitations, and shark fetishism falls outside the scope — delivered with mock-legal sincerity. The 'jollies to Jaws' alliteration is a bonus.
jokes.explanation: 'Gets his jollies to Jaws' is excellent alliterative writing — the phrase is memorable and funny. The vow-parsing logic is a great comic argument. High quotability.

jokes.text: Rachel's story about dating a guy who wanted to pretend he was an archaeologist who unfroze a 'naughty cavewoman' from a block of ice
jokes.setup: Rachel is explaining that men have strange sexual interests Monica can't understand
jokes.punchline: Her example is so specific and elaborate it's clearly a real memory — and the archaeologist/ice detail is absurd enough to be hilarious on its own
jokes.explanation: The specificity of 'archaeologist' + 'naughty cavewoman' + 'block of ice' escalating into an increasingly elaborate sexual roleplay is the joke. Each additional detail is funnier. Sets up an excellent callback.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: So Vikram and I, we spent weeks perfecting kite design. We'd test them in the Himalayas at dawn.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: And actually, that's where Vikram met Oprah. She was doing a spiritual retreat, and they dated for about six months.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: He taught her everything about aerodynamics. She taught him about daytime television. It was a beautiful exchange.

jokes.text: "Are you talking about my brother?" "I didn't disguise that very well, did I?"
jokes.setup: Rachel has told an elaborate story about a past sexual roleplay as if it were anonymous
jokes.punchline: Monica instantly recognizes it as Ross — the archaeologist detail is too specific. Rachel's sheepish admission that her disguise failed is the topper.
jokes.explanation: Among the episode's very best jokes. The callback works on multiple levels: (1) of course it's Ross — he's a paleontologist, not an archaeologist, but close enough; (2) the revelation makes the previous joke retroactively funnier; (3) 'I didn't disguise that very well, did I?' is perfect economy — it's Rachel acknowledging her failure while the audience is still processing the reveal. High craft, high impact, highly quotable.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: I'm gonna be alone forever. I'm gonna end up being one of those people that, like, feeds pigeons in Washington Square Park, and wears a visor.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Actually, you know what? I'm gonna lead a walking tour. A walking tour of New York City... for sexy European women.

jokes.text: "You've slept with all the women in NY, and now you're going around again?"
jokes.setup: Joey mentions he slept with a woman he went on a date with and didn't remember
jokes.punchline: Rachel suggests he's literally cycled through all available women in New York and is now on a second rotation
jokes.explanation: Good Joey mythology joke — the idea that he has literally exhausted the female population of New York is an enjoyable absurdism. Quick and efficient.

dialogue.speaker: Mike
dialogue.line: Ross, you've got to stop coming over here. You're here more than I am.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: I know, but Monica lives here.

dialogue.speaker: Mike
dialogue.line: I know Monica lives here. I'm married to her.

jokes.text: "She didn't remember sleeping with me!" "You don't remember sleeping with her." "But she should remember sleeping with me. I am very memorable!"
jokes.setup: Joey is upset that the woman doesn't remember their previous encounter
jokes.punchline: Rachel's logic trap — he doesn't remember her either — is immediately countered by Joey's sincere belief in his own memorability
jokes.explanation: Three-line structure where the middle line is a perfect trap and the final line springs Joey's character-specific escape. His total blind spot to his own hypocrisy — delivered with complete sincerity — is excellent Joey comedy. Great economy and character integration.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Oh my God, yes! Vikram called me yesterday. He was so sweet. He said he misses me and wants to get back together.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Wait, what? He called you?

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Yeah, he was like, 'Phoebe, I made a huge mistake letting you go.' And I was like, 'Vikram, you're so dreamy.'

jokes.text: "You guys know." "How do we know? We've never slept with you." "And whose fault is that?"
jokes.setup: Joey claims his friends can attest to his memorability in bed
jokes.punchline: Monica and Rachel note they've never slept with him; Joey blames THEM for this — genuinely aggrieved
jokes.explanation: 'And whose fault is that?' is a perfect Joey punchline — four words, complete sincerity, entirely wrong. His ego is so intact that the absence of an encounter is the WOMEN'S failure. Economical and in character.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: You remember me?

dialogue.speaker: Woman
dialogue.line: Of course! You're that guy from that thing!

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Yes! Finally, someone remembers me!

jokes.text: "I never have an off night. Okay? Although, sometimes if I'm a little bloated, I don't feel that sexy. But even then, I'm better than most!"
jokes.setup: Joey denies ever having an off night in bed
jokes.punchline: He immediately qualifies this with a very specific and very human vulnerability — bloating — before rallying back to self-confidence
jokes.explanation: The joke has great internal structure: bold claim → specific, vulnerable qualification → reassertion of superiority. 'Bloated' is the perfect word — it's so mundane against his sexual bravado. The 'better than most' recovery is the ideal Joey note to end on.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: He had these really intense eyes, and Emma has the exact same eyes, and I just couldn't look at her without thinking of him.

jokes.text: "You're both so slutty, you don't remember who you slept with. You're made for each other."
jokes.setup: Monica is trying to help Joey move past his hurt feelings about the forgotten encounter
jokes.punchline: Her 'helpful' reframe is essentially calling both of them promiscuous amnesiacs — delivered as genuine advice
jokes.explanation: Functional insult-as-advice. Monica's bluntness is well-used here, though the joke is a bit easy.

dialogue.speaker: Mike
dialogue.line: Wait, wait, wait. So Vikram and Rachel... and he's also a glue sniffer?

dialogue.speaker: Mike
dialogue.line: That's not a relationship problem, that's a chemical dependency problem!

jokes.text: "No salt! Bloaty!"
jokes.setup: Joey has just admitted that bloating affects his sexual confidence
jokes.punchline: He immediately stops himself from salting his food — the character is now actively managing the bloating concern in real time
jokes.explanation: Two words. 'Bloaty' as a self-designated nickname for his bloated state is an inspired coinage. The immediate behavioral follow-through (stopping mid-salt) makes it a physical callback that earns a big laugh. Exceptional economy — possibly the best punchline-to-word ratio in the episode. Highly quotable.

dialogue.speaker: Mike
dialogue.line: I don't have a substance abuse problem.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Really?

dialogue.speaker: Mike
dialogue.line: Well, I mean, I smell Magic Markers occasionally.

jokes.text: "Joey? You don't think sharks are sexy, do you?"
jokes.setup: Monica is processing the shark revelation about Chandler; she asks Joey for a sanity check
jokes.punchline: The question itself is the joke — asking someone point-blank 'do you think sharks are sexy?' in a coffee shop
jokes.explanation: Good use of the running gag — Monica has to genuinely check with Joey, which is both funny and says something about her worldview. Sets up a great follow-up.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Mike, I love you, but I have to ask... do you ever worry that you use Magic Markers too much?

dialogue.speaker: Mike
dialogue.line: What? No, I don't think so.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Because I've noticed you're always smelling them, and I'm just concerned about your health.

dialogue.speaker: Mike
dialogue.line: Phoebe, I'm fine. It's not like I'm addicted or anything.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Okay, but just promise me you'll be careful. I don't want to lose you to the markers.

jokes.text: Joey, then asked if sharks are sexy, says 'No.' Long beat. Then: 'Wait a minute. What was the Little Mermaid?'
jokes.setup: Monica asks Joey if he thinks sharks are sexy (testing the Chandler theory). Joey firmly says no.
jokes.punchline: He immediately has second thoughts — 'What was the Little Mermaid?' — suggesting Ariel's fish-tail may qualify.
jokes.explanation: One of the best jokes in the episode. The pivot from confident denial to 'Wait a minute. What was the Little Mermaid?' is brilliantly timed and deeply character-appropriate. Joey's honest self-examination leads him to a genuinely startling personal revelation, delivered with total sincerity. The reference is perfect — not just 'fish' but specifically 'The Little Mermaid,' which implies a childhood/teen attraction that has just resurfaced. Very quotable, high rewatch value.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Vikram!

jokes.text: "No. Wait a minute. Wait — what was the Little Mermaid?"
jokes.setup: Joey denies finding sharks sexy
jokes.punchline: He immediately reconsiders, citing The Little Mermaid as a data point — suggesting Ariel may have been a gateway fish-attraction
jokes.explanation: Exceptional joke. Joey's immediate pivot from 'No' to genuine philosophical reconsideration of The Little Mermaid as evidence of latent fish attraction is both absurd and completely in character. The writing trusts the audience to make the leap. The specific reference — not 'cartoons' but The Little Mermaid — is perfect. This is one of the episode's best jokes: original, economical, deeply character-specific, and highly quotable.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: You know what time it is?

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: What?

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: It's sex o'clock.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Shouldn't that be on the hour?

jokes.text: Ross: 'Oh boy. You got mad at that part.' — after Phoebe reacts to him visiting Mike
jokes.setup: Phoebe is horrified to learn Ross went to visit Mike unprompted.
jokes.punchline: Ross's calm, analytical 'Oh boy. You got mad at that part.' — implying he anticipated she might not be mad but misjudged which part would set her off.
jokes.explanation: Ross's calm cataloguing of Phoebe's anger — 'You got mad at that part' — implies he was mentally tracking which of his several terrible decisions would trigger her. Classic Ross oblivious-but-self-aware comedy.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Okay, so I got you some videos. I know how much you love sharks, so I also got some piranha documentaries, and some killer whale specials...

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Whoa, whoa, whoa. Monica, I don't have a shark fetish.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Oh. Well, I've already rented them, so...

jokes.text: "If you hadn't just had a baby with my best friend, I swear to Lucifer, a rabid dog would be feasting on your danglers right now!"
jokes.setup: Phoebe learns Ross told Mike she'd never been in a serious relationship
jokes.punchline: Her threat is so specific and theatrical — 'swear to Lucifer,' 'danglers' — that it's more absurdist poetry than real anger
jokes.explanation: One of the episode's standout lines. 'Swear to Lucifer' (not God) and 'danglers' (the best possible euphemism) make this a Phoebe-specific threat that couldn't come from any other character. The qualifying clause — 'if you hadn't just had a baby with my best friend' — adds a layer of twisted logic that makes it even funnier. The specificity of 'rabid dog feasting' elevates this above a generic threat. Very high character integration and originality.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: You don't want to watch shark videos? Fine! I can fill the tub with water and pretend to be a shark.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: I'll even do the dorsal fin thing with my hand!

jokes.text: "He's a kite designer. And he used to date Oprah."
jokes.setup: Ross is trying to flesh out the fake Vikram to make Phoebe's fictional relationship sound impressive
jokes.punchline: He lands on 'kite designer' (an absurdly niche and not-particularly-impressive profession) and then escalates to 'used to date Oprah' — an addition so wild it undermines itself
jokes.explanation: The two details are perfectly chosen: 'kite designer' is specific enough to sound like it could be real but ridiculous enough to seem invented, and 'dated Oprah' is an impossible escalation that reveals Ross has completely lost the plot of his own lie.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: So let me get this straight - you have a thing for angry sharks?

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: What? No! Monica, that's insane!

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Then explain the website history, Chandler. Angry sharks. That's your thing.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Those were just... educational documentaries!

jokes.text: "So I'll just be alone forever. You know, all right, it'll be fine. I'll go on walking tours with widows and lesbians."
jokes.setup: Phoebe resolves to be honest with Mike about her lack of relationship history, anticipating he'll leave
jokes.punchline: She catastrophizes her future — not just alone, but specifically on walking tours with 'widows and lesbians' — a very specific demographic she has apparently already scouted
jokes.explanation: The specific demographic — 'widows and lesbians' — is the joke. It's not just 'alone'; it's this specific, clearly-imagined lonely-singles walking tour. The word choice is very Phoebe: non-judgmental, specific, and oddly poignant. High originality and character integration.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: No, no, no, I was watching a very important documentary. It was called 'Lesbian Writers Workshop.'

jokes.text: "I'm trying to remember the last time I opened a door and you weren't there."
jokes.setup: Ross shows up at Mike's door again
jokes.punchline: Mike's dry observation — delivered to a near-stranger — implies Ross has been camped outside his apartment
jokes.explanation: Good callback to the earlier joke about Ross's obsessive visits. Mike's dry delivery makes the growing weirdness of the Ross-Mike relationship funny. Economical and well-timed.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: I really appreciate how understanding and supportive you've been.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Well, I've had three margaritas.

jokes.text: "Vikram just called." — Ross pretending Vikram called Phoebe
jokes.setup: Ross is trying to maintain the Vikram fiction in front of Mike
jokes.punchline: He announces that the man he invented has just phoned — committing to the lie with no exit strategy
jokes.explanation: The joke is in the commitment — Ross has gone so far into the lie that the fictional character is now making phone calls. Sets up the extended Vikram elaboration that follows.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: You know, Joey, I've been thinking about what we talked about. These meaningless relationships, they're not really fulfilling. You need something deeper, something real.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Whoa, whoa, whoa. Ross, that's great for you, but this is working out pretty well for me.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: I mean, I'm happy! I'm meeting people, I'm having fun. Why would I want to change that?

jokes.text: Mike announces: 'Vikram just called.' — taking up Vikram as fact
jokes.setup: Phoebe is about to come clean about Vikram not being real. Mike opens the door.
jokes.punchline: 'Vikram just called.' — Mike has apparently been in contact with the fictional Vikram.
jokes.explanation: One of the episode's best structural jokes. The reveal that Mike has been speaking to 'Vikram' (a person who doesn't exist) is perfectly timed — it arrives just as Phoebe was about to confess, maximally complicating her situation. Three words carry enormous comedic payload. The structure is excellent: setup established episodes earlier (Vikram invented), expectation subverted (Phoebe about to come clean), then blindsided by this escalation. Near-maximum economy.

jokes.text: Joey demanding Hayley recognize him while systematically pointing to locations in her apartment: "We had sex here, here, here... Not there."
jokes.setup: Joey is trying to prove to Hayley that they've slept together by jogging her memory
jokes.punchline: His memory aid is an apartment sex-location tour — pointing to each spot — which is both absurd and oddly specific. The 'not there' exception is a callback to his earlier observation.
jokes.explanation: Pays off the earlier furniture-inventory joke. The tour-guide approach to memory recovery is very Joey, and the callback to 'not there' earns a bigger laugh for attentive viewers. Good payoff structure.

jokes.text: "My God, woman! How many people have you been with not to remember this?"
jokes.setup: Hayley still doesn't remember sleeping with Joey despite his apartment tour
jokes.punchline: Joey — who also didn't remember — is outraged at her promiscuity and lack of memory, completely missing that he's the same
jokes.explanation: The hypocrisy is entirely in character and entirely committed. Joey's indignation is proportional to how oblivious he is — which is what makes it funny.

jokes.text: "Hey, Hayley. We really gotta fix that doorknob." — a third party walks in
jokes.setup: Joey is in mid-confrontation demanding Hayley remember him
jokes.punchline: A man casually walks in and mentions fixing the doorknob — implying a domestic familiarity with Hayley that contextualizes her situation (and further punctures Joey's ego)
jokes.explanation: The doorknob line is a great naturalistic punchline that lands Joey's ego a second blow. The casualness of the intrusion ('we really gotta fix that doorknob') implies familiarity — he may be a boyfriend — which makes Joey's confrontation even more awkward.

jokes.text: "I slept with you!" — Hayley recognizes Joey the moment she sees the other man
jokes.setup: Joey has been trying to get Hayley to remember him; she's been blank
jokes.punchline: The other man's arrival triggers her memory — implying she now has a framework to place Joey in context, or that jealousy unlocked the memory
jokes.explanation: The timing is the joke — she remembers the moment a third party arrives. Well-constructed comic beat.

jokes.text: "And you obviously remember me! Hey, I still got it! So we're good. I'll let myself out."
jokes.setup: Hayley's recognition (screamed in shock) proves she remembered him
jokes.punchline: Joey interprets her horrified exclamation as validation — takes it as a compliment, declares 'we're good,' and leaves. His exit is completely unbothered.
jokes.explanation: Perfect Joey exit. 'I still got it' + 'So we're good' + 'I'll let myself out' — three beats of complete self-satisfaction in a situation that is objectively chaotic. The blissful obliviousness is peak Joey. The resolution of an entire subplot in three lines delivered with zero self-awareness is excellent sitcom craft.

jokes.text: "But Emma's birth certificate might say 'Geller'... but her eyes say 'Mukherjee.'"
jokes.setup: Ross is elaborating on the Vikram fiction — Vikram slept with Rachel; Phoebe points out Rachel just had a baby with Ross
jokes.punchline: Phoebe improvises further: the baby's eyes betray Vikram's paternity — a completely fabricated soap-opera twist delivered with Phoebe's signature conviction
jokes.explanation: The joke has two layers: the absurdity of the invented scandal, and the specificity of 'Mukherjee' — using Vikram's implied Indian surname to suggest DNA evidence visible in a baby's eyes. Phoebe has taken Ross's lie and run so far with it that it now implicates an infant. The delivery of 'her eyes say Mukherjee' is a great comic construction.

jokes.text: "That is so wrong. And on top of that, he's a glue sniffer?"
jokes.setup: Phoebe is elaborating on the Vikram mythology — adding detail after detail
jokes.punchline: Mike accepts all of it and adds his own outrage — Vikram is now also a glue sniffer, apparently added to the fiction offscreen
jokes.explanation: Mike's earnest indignation at a fictional character's substance abuse problem is funny. The escalation of Vikram's flaws — kite designer → dated Oprah → slept with Rachel → glue sniffer — is well-paced.

jokes.text: "I know. But he calls, and my heart goes to him. You know, that bastard is one smooth-talking freelance kite designer."
jokes.setup: Phoebe is playing along with the Vikram fiction, defending her feelings for him
jokes.punchline: The phrase 'smooth-talking freelance kite designer' — a romantic archetype nobody has ever used before — delivered with the same gravity one might reserve for 'charming international businessman'
jokes.explanation: The phrase 'smooth-talking freelance kite designer' is a small masterpiece of absurd comedy. The word 'freelance' does enormous work — it's both realistic-sounding and pathetically specific. Phoebe's sincere delivery of this as an irresistible quality is very much in character. Among the episode's best individual lines.

jokes.text: "I think there's somebody better out there for you. I mean, you know, I'm — I'm not saying me, but... maybe... me."
jokes.setup: Mike has been listening to the Vikram drama and seems to have feelings for Phoebe
jokes.punchline: He tries to be subtle about suggesting himself as an alternative, fails, then commits anyway — the two-step is the joke
jokes.explanation: Sweet and funny — the self-correction mid-sentence is a well-worn structure but executed with the right hesitancy. More charming than hilarious.

jokes.text: "And you don't have to worry about glue-sniffing with me. Although, I do smell the occasional Magic Marker."
jokes.setup: Mike is differentiating himself from the fictional Vikram's flaws
jokes.punchline: He volunteers that he does occasionally sniff Magic Markers — an unnecessary and oddly specific partial admission
jokes.explanation: Perfect callback structure — he distinguishes himself from the glue sniffer but immediately offers a lesser equivalent. 'The occasional Magic Marker' as a romantic reassurance is an absurd and original construction. The 'occasional' qualifier is doing a lot of funny work. Well-earned and quotable.

jokes.text: Phoebe admits the truth: 'I've never celebrated an anniversary'
jokes.setup: Phoebe is confessing her full relationship history to Mike — she's never had a long-term relationship, never lived with a man
jokes.punchline: The final admission — she's never 'celebrated an anniversary' — lands as the most pathetically specific detail
jokes.explanation: The escalating specificity — no long-term relationship, no living together, not even an anniversary — works as a list joke, with 'anniversary' being the most mundane and therefore saddest item.

jokes.text: Mike: 'And be a little concerned about the Magic Markers?' — after kissing Phoebe again
jokes.setup: Mike and Phoebe are negotiating whether they can hold multiple feelings simultaneously about the situation.
jokes.punchline: He adds the Magic Marker concern to the list of coexisting emotional states, treating his mild solvent habit as an equal item alongside more significant relationship feelings.
jokes.explanation: The Magic Marker callback lands here because it's placed at the most earnest moment of their budding romance — which makes it both funny and endearing. Mike's willingness to include his marker habit in his list of things she should know is weirdly sweet.

jokes.text: Ross calls Vikram's voicemail: a mock message from the fictional kite-designing ex-boyfriend
jokes.setup: Phoebe has revealed the Vikram lie to Mike; Ross's phone rings — 'This is Vikram'
jokes.punchline: Ross has set up a Vikram voicemail as backup support for the lie — the fictional character has a working phone
jokes.explanation: The reveal that Ross went so far as to set up a Vikram voicemail is a great topper on the entire Vikram subplot. His over-preparation in service of a lie he already gave up on is very Ross.

jokes.text: "Well, well, well. It must be 5 o'clock in Tulsa... because it's 'sex o'clock' in NYC!"
jokes.setup: Monica has changed into something sexy to surprise Chandler upon her return
jokes.punchline: The 'sex o'clock' time-zone pun — announced with full presentation energy
jokes.explanation: A broad pun joke that's more cringe-worthy than funny on paper. Gets a mild laugh from the commitment of the character, but the wordplay itself isn't strong. This is the kind of joke that works better in the room than on paper.

jokes.text: Monica puts on a shark documentary for Chandler as 'sexy' viewing
jokes.setup: Monica is trying to participate in Chandler's shark fetish, so she's found a shark video
jokes.punchline: She presents the shark documentary — 'The great white...' — as foreplay material, completely earnest
jokes.explanation: Monica's sincere effort to accommodate the fictional fetish is both sweet and very funny. Her earnestness in serving up a shark documentary as erotic material is a great character note — she's pragmatic even about bizarre sex stuff.

jokes.text: "Is this — is this not the good part? Do you want me to fast-forward to something... toothier?"
jokes.setup: Chandler is clearly confused and not aroused by the shark documentary Monica has queued up
jokes.punchline: Monica offers to fast-forward to a 'toothier' part — applying the vocabulary of pornographic escalation to a wildlife documentary
jokes.explanation: 'Something toothier' is a brilliantly absurd euphemism — applying erotic-escalation language to shark anatomy. The word 'toothier' does enormous work: it's simultaneously the correct word for shark content and completely wrong as a sexual euphemism. High originality and economy. Very quotable.

jokes.text: "Or does it always have to be sharks?"
jokes.setup: Monica is trying to understand the fetish and whether Chandler would accept crocodiles as a substitute
jokes.punchline: The question implies she's already doing comparative fetish research — 'do you have a type, or is it broad aquatic predators?'
jokes.explanation: Monica's earnest inquiry about the specificity of the fetish is funny because it treats the question as logistically important. The word 'always' implies she's categorizing this as a known preference requiring accommodation.

jokes.text: "Do you want me to get into the tub and... thrash?"
jokes.setup: Monica is brainstorming ways to satisfy what she believes is Chandler's shark fetish
jokes.punchline: She offers to simulate a shark attack in the bathtub — the word 'thrash' as a performance direction is the perfect absurd detail
jokes.explanation: Among the episode's best jokes. 'Thrash' is the perfect word — it's exactly what a shark victim would do, and Monica saying it with absolute sincerity while framing it as a sexual service is both absurd and deeply sweet. The economy is exceptional: one word ('thrash') contains the entire joke. Highly quotable.

jokes.text: "Oh, my God! When you came in, I switched the channel. I was just watching regular porn." "Really?" "Yes. Just some good, old-fashioned, American, girl-on-girl action."
jokes.setup: Chandler finally confesses the truth — he wasn't watching shark porn, he switched channels when she walked in
jokes.punchline: He was watching conventional pornography — specifically girl-on-girl content — and frames it with mock-patriotic pride: 'good, old-fashioned, American'
jokes.explanation: The reveal lands on two levels: the shark subplot is debunked (great misdirect payoff), and the 'good, old-fashioned, American, girl-on-girl action' framing is a great comic construction. The patriotic adjectives applied to lesbian pornography is a classic Chandler tone — over-explaining in a way that makes it funnier. Well-structured resolution to the episode's central mystery.

jokes.text: "Can I tell you how happy that makes me?"
jokes.setup: Chandler has just revealed he was watching girl-on-girl porn rather than a shark documentary
jokes.punchline: Monica is genuinely relieved and happy — girl-on-girl porn is vastly preferable to shark fetishism in her view
jokes.explanation: The inversion of expected reactions — Monica being delighted about the conventional porn — is the punchline. It's earned by the entire shark subplot. Great economy.

jokes.text: Monica: 'Can I tell you how happy that makes me?'
jokes.setup: Chandler reveals he was watching girl-on-girl porn, not shark porn.
jokes.punchline: Monica's heartfelt relief — genuinely happy that it's 'just' lesbian porn rather than a shark fetish — is a great inversion of normal relationship dynamics.
jokes.explanation: Monica's genuine joy at this revelation is the right cap to the reversal. Normally 'my husband watches lesbian porn' isn't good news; here it's a profound relief. The inversion is well-earned.

jokes.text: "I'm very, very drunk right now."
jokes.setup: Chandler asks where Monica finds the strength and understanding to accommodate such a strange request
jokes.punchline: She explains: she's very drunk. The willingness was chemically induced, not saintly.
jokes.explanation: The best single punchline in the episode. Five words that completely recontextualize her behavior in the entire hotel scene. The structure is perfect: Chandler asks a sincere, increasingly reverent question about Monica's character — and the answer is 'I'm very, very drunk.' The 'very, very' intensifier adds rhythm and self-awareness. The setup has been building for two minutes; the payoff is instantaneous. Comparable to the 8+ anchor examples in economy and structure.

jokes.text: Joey's talking-head setup: "Ordinarily, I would talk to her, but my confidence is shaken. Did I sleep with her? Did I not sleep with her?"
jokes.setup: Joey is processing his crisis of confidence about the woman who didn't remember him
jokes.punchline: His entire romantic confidence is predicated on being remembered — without that, he doesn't know how to proceed
jokes.explanation: Setup joke for the episode's final beat. Character-consistent but not a strong joke on its own.

jokes.text: Ross repeats almost verbatim to Joey what he said to Phoebe at the opening — that Joey is in his 30s and has never been in a long-term relationship, going from woman to woman
jokes.setup: Ross is trying to give Joey dating advice
jokes.punchline: He delivers essentially the same speech he accidentally gave Phoebe — the same words that destroyed her confidence — not realizing the pattern
jokes.explanation: Good structural callback — the episode mirrors its opening. Ross is about to repeat his mistake, and the audience sees it coming. Works as a running-gag payoff.

jokes.text: "You're right. I love my life!"
jokes.setup: Ross has just delivered his devastating 'going from meaningless experience to meaningless experience' speech, apparently expecting Joey to be upset
jokes.punchline: Joey hears the same words that destroyed Phoebe — and takes them as a compliment, declaring his love of life
jokes.explanation: Exceptional callback payoff. The entire episode has been framed by Ross accidentally devastating Phoebe with this speech. Repeating it to Joey — and having Joey respond with uncomplicated joy — is the perfect structural bookend. It's character-perfect (Joey genuinely is happy in this life), it pays off the A-plot callback, and 'I love my life!' is a great topper. The contrast with Phoebe's reaction earns this a high score. Best use of callback structure in the episode.

jokes.text: Joey's response to the existential speech: 'You're right. I love my life!'
jokes.setup: Ross has just delivered what he intends as a wake-up-call speech about meaningless relationships.
jokes.punchline: Joey hears it as a glowing endorsement of his lifestyle and is thrilled. 'I love my life!'
jokes.explanation: One of the two best jokes in the episode. The callback structure is perfect: the same words that sent Phoebe into existential crisis are received by Joey as a beautiful description of his life. 'I love my life!' is four words that deliver an enormous laugh and perfectly characterize Joey. The contrast with Phoebe's reaction (Joke #5) makes this funnier on rewatch — the same speech, two characters, opposite reactions. Near-perfect structure, economy, and character integration.

jokes.text: "I actually did sleep with her." — Joey's tag line, delivered deadpan after everything
jokes.setup: Joey declared 'I love my life!' — suggesting he'd made peace with everything. The scene appeared over.
jokes.punchline: He adds, as a quiet afterthought: 'I actually did sleep with her.' — the memory has finally returned, long after it matters
jokes.explanation: Perfect tag line structure. After the episode's resolution — Joey is happy, the shark stuff is resolved — this five-word afterthought lands as the final beat. It resolves the Joey subplot completely (he DID sleep with her, confirming his memory was right all along) while also being funny because: (1) it took this long for him to remember; (2) the confirmation is completely pointless by now; (3) the deadpan delivery after 'I love my life!' suggests his brain finally processed it in the background. Exceptional economy and structure for a closing tag.

Also, Joey goes on a date with an attractive woman and discovers that her apartment seems really familiar, although he doesn't remember sleeping with her before.
